chunks: My father (may Allah have mercy on him) narrated to us. He said: Abdullah ibn Ja'far al-Himyari narrated to us. He said: Ya'qub ibn Yazid narrated to us from Muhammad ibn Abi 'Umayr from Hisham ibn Salim from Sulayman ibn Khalid from al-Sadiq Ja'far ibn Muhammad, from his father, from his forefathers (peace be upon them): The Commander of the Faithful (peace be upon him) said:

All goodness is gathered in three qualities: sight, silence, and speech. Every sight devoid of consideration is negligence. Every silence devoid of thought is heedlessness. Every speech devoid of remembrance [of Allah] is prattle.
Blessed is the one whose sight is a lesson, whose silence is contemplation, and whose speech is remembrance — who cries over his sin and from whose evil the people are safe.

key_terms.اعتبار: Consideration, taking lessons from what one observes
key_terms.السكوت: Silence — purposeful quiet accompanied by reflection
key_terms.الكلام: Speech — meaningful words accompanied by divine remembrance
key_terms.النظر: Sight/observation — looking with purpose and taking lessons
key_terms.طوبى: Blessedness, a state of spiritual felicity
key_terms.لغو: Idle talk, vain speech lacking substance

ai.seo_question: What are the three qualities of goodness according to Imam Ali?
ai.summary: Imam Ali (AS), in a narration transmitted through the chain of Imams, presents a profound teaching on mindfulness: all goodness is contained in three faculties — sight, silence, and speech — but only when each is coupled with its proper spiritual quality: consideration, thought, and remembrance of God respectively. Without these, they become negligence, heedlessness, and idle talk. The teaching concludes with a portrait of the ideal believer who embodies all three qualities.

en.bilal-muhammad: My father (rh) narrated to us. He said: `Abdullah b. Ja`far al-Himyari narrated to us. He said: Ya`qub b. Yazid narrated to us from Muhammad b. Abi `Umayr from Hisham b. Salim from Sulayman b. Khalid from al-Sadiq Ja`far b. Muhammad from his father from his forefathers (as). Amir al-Mu'minin (as) said:

All goodness is in three actions: sight, silence, and speech. Every sight that is devoid of consideration is negligence. Every silence that is devoid of thought is heedlessness. Every speech that is devoid of the remembrance [of Allah] is prattle.
Blessed is he in whose sight is consideration, and in whose silence is thought, and in whose words is remembrance – who cries over his mistakes and from whose evil the people are safe.
